claims.wording: Under fixed processing capacity, increasing irrelevant information eventually reduces decision quality.
claims.falsifier: Decision quality does not decline across preregistered overload conditions with fixed capacity.

claims.wording: Action-relative meaning is the improvement in optimal expected action value produced by preserving an observation.
claims.falsifier: Definition is rejected if the operational quantity cannot be assigned a declared action set, utility, and conditioning state.

claims.wording: Attention mechanisms persist when expected action improvement exceeds their declared operating and switching costs.
claims.falsifier: Observed persistence is unrelated to net action value across controlled cost conditions.

claims.wording: Heterogeneous attention improves novelty detection under regime change when minority observations survive adjudication.
claims.falsifier: Heterogeneous and homogeneous systems are indistinguishable on preregistered novelty detection, or heterogeneity harms without a cost tradeoff.

claims.wording: A newly useful market distinction loses private excess value as attention to it diffuses.
claims.falsifier: Excess value does not decay with independently measured diffusion of attention, after costs and selection are controlled.

claims.wording: Labels alter feature weighting and valuation by transmitting reusable attention priors.
claims.falsifier: Matched label manipulations produce no reliable change in preregistered feature weighting or valuation outcomes.

claims.wording: Historically invested categories update more slowly under contradictory evidence than neutral new categories.
claims.falsifier: Update speed is equal after controlling for baseline familiarity, task difficulty, and evidence strength.
